title: External-Review Close-Out Value — Insurance Claim (Third-Party Billing) Reimbursement Method
content:
**Coverage of the close-out.** The close-out of an Insurance Claim (Third-Party Billing) covers the charges of the claim's hospital account (the Hospital Account (Encounter Billing)) except the diagnostic tests (revenue codes 0483, 0730, 0300 and 0350, and the contrast code Q9967 under revenue code 0636), which stay payable, and the self-administered drugs (revenue code 0637), which it never values; it covers the small items on Riverbend's observation and emergency small-item list that pass the small-item test (a listed code whose charges are above 0.00 and at or below the payer class's small-denial write-off amount) only while no below-threshold write-off entry stands on the claim, and it always covers a listed code that does not pass.

**Reading.** Within what it covers, the observation lines (revenue code 0762), the infusion (code 96365 under revenue code 0260), the heparin (code J1644 under revenue code 0636), the general pharmacy (revenue code 0250), the medical-surgical supplies (revenue code 0270, apart from the listed saline flush A4216) and the sterile supplies (revenue code 0272) are each read by their charges, and everything else as the remaining charges.

**Value.** The close-out value is the charges it covers multiplied by the payer class's expected allowed percentage of charges. Each group of lines is valued first, never above the billed charges of the lines it values (Riverbend's agreements pay the lesser of the scheduled amount and the billed charges); a multiplier of the total applies after them, then the recovery limit, and the total is then rounded once.

**Recovery limit.** The close-out never writes off more than the payer has recovered on the claim, the total of its recovery entries, less the below-threshold write-offs already on the claim, and never less than 0.00; with no recovery entry on the claim it is 0.00.

**When it is fixed.** The external-review close-out is fixed only after the payer's recovery of its payment stands as a recovery entry on the claim. The external-review close-out is fixed only after the small items that pass the small-item test carry their below-threshold write-off entry on the claim.

**Rounding.** The close-out value is rounded to the nearest cent once, on the final total, and when it is 0.00 no entry is written.

**Worked example (hypothetical, payer class modeled at 50%).** Account charges 8,000.00, of which diagnostic tests 1,500.00 and self-administered drugs 100.00; no passing small item. Covered: 6,400.00; at 50% → 3,200.00. Recovery entries of 2,000.00 with no below-threshold write-off limit the close-out to 2,000.00.
